fields.acceptance: Unit tests in internal/textref: a reference starts with @ at the start of the text or after whitespace or an opening ( or [ and is followed by a handle (lower-case words joined by single dashes) or an ID or 4+ character ID prefix; darin@hey.com, checkout@v7 and '@key' contain no reference; @@ yields a literal @ and is never a reference; the resolver returns @@{<full ID>} as unresolved and flagged escaped and an @{<full ID>} the lookup does not map as unresolved, writes both as @<full ID> without braces so the formatter shows neither as a reference, and still turns @@{ID} into the literal @{ID}; a resolver given a lookup rewrites every reference, @{<ID>} included, to @{<full ID>} and returns each unresolved one with its offset, so @{BOGUS} is unresolved; a formatter treats only @{<26-character ID>} in stored text as a reference, shows it as @<handle> when the lookup gives a live node's handle and as @{<full ID>} when the node is retired or the lookup has none, and treats stored '@{ID}', '@{BOGUS}' and '@{<full ID>}' as literal text shown as '@@{ID}' etc.; and shows a stored literal @ that would start a reference (from @@word) as @@; a fuzz test checks that formatting resolved text, literal @ included, and resolving it again yields the same stored text
fields.statement: One pure package, internal/textref, finds the references in a text and turns them both ways: @handle, @<ID or 4+ character ID prefix> and @{<ID>} to stored @{<full ID>}, and stored @{<full 26-character ID>} back to @<current handle> of a live node (or @{<full ID>} for a retired or missing one); any other @{...} in stored text is literal, with @@ for a literal @ both ways (the formatter re-escapes a literal @ that would start a reference), except that stored text never holds a literal @{<full 26-character ID>} (decision text-ref-stored-escape): the resolver returns an @@{<full ID>} escape among the unresolved, flagged as escaped, returns an @{<full ID>} the lookup does not map as unresolved, and writes both as @<full ID> without braces

fields.acceptance: text-refs-write.txtar: rhiza add capability with statement 'Builds on @other' stores @{<other's full ID>} in the log entry; an ID prefix reference stores the full ID; a reference to a node of the write's own change set resolves, one to a node of another unlanded change set or a newly referenced retired node does not; after other is retired, rhiza set of a field that already stores @{<other's ID>} with input @{<other's full ID>} keeps it, and adding that reference to a different field or node is refused; quote, quote_where, wording and a source's fields are stored verbatim; '@@' stores a literal @; an input @@{<full ID>} is refused with code usage (exit 2), naming it and its field, and writes nothing, while @@<full ID> stores the literal @<full ID>; an input @{<other's full ID>} stores the same ID, and an input @{BOGUS} is refused like any unresolvable reference; an unresolvable reference exits 4 with code not_found naming each bad reference and its field, with a next saying to fix the handle or write @@, and writes nothing; --dry-run reports the same refusal; the same file through rhiza apply behaves the same; rhiza note add with an @word naming no node is written and shown as @@word, and one with an @{<full ID>} naming no node and an @@{<full ID>} stores each as @<full ID> without braces; describe-golden.txtar is regenerated if a request or response type changes; the rhiza guide's skill text tells agents to write @handle to refer to a node. Engine writes (decision text-ref-engine-writes): a run session's question (TestAddQuestionLenientRefs) whose text holds an @word naming no node is written, the run goes on, and it is shown as @@word, while one holding @<existing handle> stores @{<full ID>}; text-refs-engine-writes.txtar: question answer behaves the same, its quote kept verbatim; run-ship-change-rebase.txtar: re-raising the same rebase conflict whose statement holds a resolvable reference writes nothing new
fields.statement: rhiza add and set, and add and set items of rhiza apply, resolve the references in every string-valued field of a node (except quote, quote_where, wording and every field of a source node) at write time and store each as @{<full ID>}, refusing the whole write when one names no node it may refer to (strict); a reference to a retired node is refused unless the field's current stored value already holds that same ID, in which case it is kept. A strict write of @@{<full 26-character ID>} is refused with a usage error (code usage, exit 2) naming it and its field, since stored text cannot hold a literal @{<full ID>} (decision text-ref-stored-escape); @@<full ID> writes the ID as literal text. Engine writes of free text (a run session's question from rhiza ask, check, leaf and review questions, interview questions, rebase-conflict questions, the Decision written by question answer, notes and ship evidence) resolve the same way but never refuse (lenient): a reference that names no node it may refer to is stored as a literal @, as if written @@, and shown as @@word, except that an unresolvable @{<full ID>} and an @@{<full ID>} are stored as @<full ID> without braces

fields.reasoning: Only @{<full 26-character ID>} counts as a stored reference (text-references-shape (2)), so storing @@{<full ID>} as the literal @{<full ID>} would read back as a reference nobody resolved: rhiza check fails it as dangling when the ID names no node, and it silently binds to the node when the ID names one, so a write that passed would leave the model wrong. A stored escape for it would need a second stored syntax and a change to every reader. Refusing in strict mode tells an author who can fix the text; the brace-less @<full ID> keeps an engine write from failing, which text-ref-engine-writes requires, keeps the ID readable, and is neither a stored nor a dangling reference. Recorded in review cycle 3, whose model check found that fix 22bd296a had changed these rules without a Decision.
fields.statement: Stored text never holds a literal @{<full 26-character ID>}, since stored text cannot tell one from a reference, so the @@ escape does not reach it. A strict write (rhiza add, rhiza set and the add and set items of rhiza apply) of @@{<full ID>} is refused with a usage error (code usage, exit 2) naming it and its field, with a next saying to refer to the node with @{<full ID>} or write the ID without braces, and writes nothing. A lenient engine write stores that escape, and any @{<full ID>} that does not resolve, as @<full ID> without braces, never refusing; it is shown as @@<full ID>. Every other @@ still writes a literal @ that is never resolved. This narrows text-references-shape (2) ('@@ writes a literal @') and text-ref-engine-writes ('as if written @@') for a full ID inside braces.
